svg.text: General arrangement · JS1-102 · revision D · 12 November 2026

Johansson Shipyard, newbuilding No. 1, rebuilt as a ro-ro freight ferry of 124.8 m for Johansson Line. As her bare ship is built from it. A proposal for the owner's approval: nothing is calculated beyond the volume under her lines.
Bow to the right, port up. Metres.
Main deck: trailers, five lanes, 5.0 m clear and more
Upper deck: trailers in the open
Watertight bulkheads at the frames named; frame spacing 0.6 m, frame 0 at the transom. Scale: the ticks are ten frames (6 m) apart.
Ro-ro freight ferry (ro-ro cargo and passenger
ship): a stern ramp, a main trailer deck, a weather
deck reached by a fixed ramp, a lower hold reached
Johansson Line; Minato to Kitano-jima and back.
Two medium-speed diesels of about 4,000 kW each,
each through a reduction gear to a
Two spade rudders; a bow thruster of about 600 kW in
Three diesel sets of about 500 kW, 450 V, 60 Hz, in
an auxiliary engine room of their own; an emergency
set in a room on the officers' deck
Main deck: five lanes of 3.0 m, 5.0 m and more
clear. Upper deck: trailers in the open, by a fixed
ramp at 1 in 8. Lower hold: cars and trailers, by a
50: eight berths in four cabins on the boat deck,
the others in the drivers' lounge
25: six officers on the officers' deck; nineteen
ratings in twelve cabins on the boat deck: six
single cabins, six across the front with two berths,
and one single cabin that takes a second
One lifeboat for 40 each side under gravity davits
on the boat deck (the port one is also the rescue
boat); three liferafts for 25 each side
Wheelhouse, wings to the ship's side
Fixed ramp to the upper deck
Head of the lower hold stair
Cargo lift to the lower hold
1.6 m above the keel: at the tank top, and where her bottom rises over it 0.6 m over her bottom; what stands on the platform at 4.0 m and the flat at 4.7 m is dashed
WHAT THE COLOURS AND THE MARKS MEAN

On the plans, in outline: the places of her deck fittings (ferry/blender/spec.py, OUTFIT). LB a lifeboat under its davits, LR a liferaft, W a windlass, MW a mooring winch, C a capstan, B bitts, V a ventilator, F a foam monitor, R a rope reel; dots are lashing pots.
Lifeboat stations: boat deck, 81.5 to 90.5 m from the transom, each side.

A 7.3 m boat for 40 under gravity davits. The house is 11.8 m wide here and the deck beside it 3.6 m and more: the boat stows inside her side and swings out over it. The boat deck is the embarkation deck. The
rail has a gap of 9.0 m at each boat. The two boats take 80, the six rafts 150: she carries 75.
Liferaft stations: boat deck, 93.0, 95.4 and 97.8 m, each side.

Three rafts in cradles at the rail each side, forward of the boats and clear of the cross passage's door (98.75 m): thrown over, or floating free. A metre of deck is left between a cradle and the house. The
rail has a gap of 1.7 m at each.
Anchor gear: forecastle, 110.8 to 115.0 m, each side 2.6 m off the centre line.

Each anchor hangs in its hawse pipe on the flare of the bow, 115.2 m from the transom and 4.0 m over the water. The pipe comes up through the forecastle deck at 114.6 m; the chain runs aft over the chain
stopper (113.7 m) to the windlass (112.0 m) and goes down its chain pipe at 112.5 m, forward of the collision bulkhead (110.4 m), inboard to the chain locker under the fore store.
Forward mooring station: forecastle, 104.5 to 123.7 m.

A mooring winch each side at 106.8 m, 2.8 m before the house, and the windlasses' warping heads. Lines leave her at six chocks in the bulwark: head lines at 119.2 m, breast lines at 110.6 m, springs at 105.6 m,

and one in the stem head on the centre line for a tug. Bitts stand beside each chock, a roller fairlead where a line turns. The spare lines are on two reels under the lee of the house front. The foremast stands
on the centre line at 116.9 m.
After mooring stations: main deck, 0 to 7.2 m, inside each casing; and the upper deck's after corners.

As the pattern has them: her weather deck aft is the helicopter deck, so the stern lines are worked from a station inside each casing on the main deck, through a mooring port in her side (2.4 to 4.8 m): a

winch, bitts, a roller fairlead at the port's sill. On the upper deck a capstan and bitts stand in each after corner, outside the helicopter deck's octagon, with a chock in her side bulwark and one in the stern
Ventilators and air pipes: upper deck, at the bulwark, outboard of the walkways.

The trunks of the engine room, the auxiliary engine room and the lower hold come up in the starboard casing, the main deck's exhaust in the port one: a mushroom ventilator stands over each, hard against the
bulwark, and 1.2 m of walkway is left inboard of it. The wing tanks' air pipes stand between them.
Helicopter deck: upper deck aft, 1.0 to 20.0 m.
A foam monitor each side on the upper deck at the helicopter deck's forward edge, beside its two stairs: it covers the whole deck from outside it.
Lashing: main deck, upper deck and lower hold.
Pots flush in the deck along the lane edges, 2.4 m apart: four rows on the main and upper decks (three beside the fixed ramp and its opening, one beside the cargo lift), three in the lower hold.
1. The lower hold is one compartment of 39.6 m, as ships of her time had it; a ship built today is not allowed that. A watertight bulkhead with a sliding door across it, or the hold as drawn.

2. Berths: 25 crew (six officers; nineteen ratings in twelve cabins, seven of them with two berths) and eight drivers in four cabins; the other 42 drivers and passengers ride in the lounge. The boat deck's house is
narrow abaft 91 m, where the lifeboats stand: more cabins need another tier.
3. The sheer begins at the front of the house (104 m), not at three quarters of her length as first asked: the house stands on a level deck.

4. Her funnels stand abaft the engines and four metres before the helicopter deck: their smoke lies over it with the wind ahead, and they stand in a helicopter's way from forward. The deck is drawn where the owner

5. Her watertight doors below the main deck are drawn hinged, as the first Chisum's were at the owner's word; a passenger ship's are to be sliding and power-operated (SOLAS II-1/13 as the yard recalls it; to be

6. Her mast is the first Chisum's, 28.9 m above the keel (23.3 m over the water): a ship of her length carries her masthead light higher, and a second one forward. A foremast is in the arrangement and not yet built.
7. The emergency generator's size: the owner's drawing names 500 kW, which is as much as one of her main sets. The room is drawn at the drawing's size.

8. The engine room has one stair up (to the port casing) and watertight doors forward and aft; a second way of escape to the deck, from its far end, is not yet in the arrangement. The room first drawn for it in the
starboard casing stood over the fresh water tanks, not over the engine room: it is the CO2 room now.
9. The CO2 room is entered from the main deck, which is an enclosed vehicle deck; the rules ask for a way in from the open deck (as the yard recalls them; to be read).
10. The uptake and the three ventilation trunks in the starboard casing have no door: the fixed ramp runs along their only wall to the deck. They are trunks, opened by bolted plates.

11. The stern ramp, raised, stands 3.4 m over the helicopter deck at its after edge: a helicopter comes in over her side, not over her stern. A ramp in two lengths that folds would end under the deck; it is drawn in
one, as the pattern has it.

Made from ferry/blender/ga.py, lines.py and spec.py by ferry/yard/drawings/ga_drawing.py. Her pattern is the Mashala class of 1977, whose arrangement was looked at and measured (ferry/yard/reference/roro-freight-ships.md); nothing is traced or copied.
